title: T3 Code messages sent while a turn runs: queued, steered, and queued too long

rows.sm: 2.3: a relayed message's lead is its typing time, ending at sent_at
rows.note: M1's 90 characters: 60 s, from 20:00:00 to its stamp.

rows.sm: 2.3: a relayed message's lead is its typing time, ending at sent_at
rows.note: M2 is sent 5 s after M1, so its lead is capped at those 5 s, 20:01:00 to 20:01:05, though 45 characters type in 30 s. Its run reaches the agent at 20:09:01, 476 s after the stamp, inside RELAY_MATCH_S, and the lead is credited at the stamp. T1 runs from 20:01:01.

rows.sm: 2.2: a steered message has no run of its own
rows.note: M3, steered into T1 at 20:04:00, earns nothing. Its agent.queue at 20:04:01 has no input in its slot, so it opens no Q anchor either.

rows.sm: 2.4: a relayed session reads after a stop, until its next relayed message or its next turn
rows.note: T1 stops at 20:09:00 and T2 starts at 20:09:01. M2 was sent before the stop, so it vouches for no reading of it, but M4, sent at 20:14:00, comes 300 s after the stop: the session reads T1's output from 20:09:00 until T2 starts, 1 s. T2's prompt then resets the bucket to its 20 s base.

rows.sm: 2.4: a relayed session reads after a stop, until its next relayed message or its next turn
rows.note: T2 stops at 20:12:00 and M4 follows 120 s later. T2 filled 20 + 20 + 30 = 70 s: 60 are read here, and M4's lead takes 20:13 before the other 10.

rows.sm: 2.3: a relayed message's lead is its typing time, ending at sent_at
rows.note: M4's 90 characters: 60 s, from 20:13:00. M2 was sent 775 s earlier.

rows.sm: 2.3: a message queued past RELAY_MATCH_S opens nothing
rows.note: 20:14:00 is in neither a window nor a turn. T4 runs from 20:14:01. M5's lead would have run from 20:14:20 to its stamp at 20:15:00, but its run reaches the agent at 20:27:01, 721 s after the stamp, so nothing pairs with it and it opens nothing.

rows.sm: 2.2 rule 4: M5's prompt has no witness
rows.note: T4 stops at 20:27:00, and no relayed message follows it. M5's prompt, unpaired, is headless, so T5 runs automated from 20:27:01.

rows.sm: 5.1: no credit and no agent running

notes: No SM section describes this case. Every row comes from SM 2.2 rule 9, 2.3 and 2.4 as docs/errata/2026-11-22-relayed-prompts.md applies them. Every credited second is level C with via_relay.
The server has no desktop, so every slot's presence is unknown, and uncredited seconds take SM 5.2's codes for such a slot.
The agent.queue at 20:04:01 assumes Claude Code reports a message T3 steers into a running turn. That is unverified, and the case credits the same either way.
